own_solution.law: Steady radial conduction in a cylindrical shell with constant k: T(r) = T1 - (T1 - T2) ln(r/r1)/ln(r2/r1); drop to r = 5 cm is 120 K * ln(5/3)/ln(3)
assumptions: boundary temperatures fixed at r1 = 3 cm (420 K) and r2 = 9 cm (300 K)
tank is thermally separate from the pipe

notes: Base: ln(5/3)=0.51083, ln3=1.09861, ratio 0.46497, x120 K = 55.80 K. With an extra 1.8 cm on the pipe (T21B1, T15F5), the outermost insulation surface is at 10.8 cm and is the one held at 300 K: 120*0.51083/ln(3.6)=120*0.51083/1.28093=47.86 K. Reading relies on 'outermost surface of the insulation' moving to the new outer radius; a reader could alternatively keep 9 cm as the 300 K surface, but 'outermost' makes the moved boundary the natural reading. k cancels from the temperature profile (C). Earlier-survey and tank sentences have no path (D). Number check: T6641, T21B1, T15F5, T8754 all state 1.8 cm; T26FA and T6E73 both state 'a further small thickness' (no number) and match each other.
